definition: A formal specification of a tool or function's name, parameters, and expected input types, provided to a model so it can correctly generate valid tool-calling requests.
details: Well-defined function signatures, often described using a schema like JSON Schema, help a model understand exactly what arguments are required and their types when deciding to invoke a particular tool.
story: Imagine handing a to-do list to a very clever intern who refuses to guess: before each step, they look around, check the result, and adjust. Think of it this way: A formal specification of a tool or function's name, parameters, and expected input types, provided to a model so it can correctly generate valid tool-calling requests. And here is the clever part: Well-defined function signatures, often described using a schema like JSON Schema, help a model understand exactly what arguments are required and their types when deciding to invoke a particular tool. It is a loop of look, act, and learn — the same way you cook from a recipe you have never tried: add, taste, correct. And that habit of checking, acting, then checking again is Function Signature (for tool use).
